name: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship (NMMSS)
provider: Ministry of Education, Government of India
benefit: Rs 12,000 per year (Rs 1,000 a month) from Class 9 to Class 12
summary: For bright students from low-income families in government, aided and local-body schools. You write the NMMS exam in Class 8; you need 55% in Class 7 (50% for SC/ST) and must keep the marks up to continue.
documents: Class 7 marksheet (and later class marksheets for renewal)
how_to_apply: Write the NMMS exam conducted by the state exam board in Class 8. If you are selected, register on the National Scholarship Portal and renew every year.
deadline_note: NMMS exam usually in December-February; NSP usually opens between July and October

name: PM YASASVI Pre-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
provider: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India
benefit: Rs 4,000 per year (verify on portal)
summary: For OBC, EBC and denotified (DNT) students in Class 9 and 10 whose family income is up to Rs 2.5 lakh a year. It is given through the state government.
documents: Bonafide certificate from school or college
how_to_apply: Tell your school headmaster you want this scholarship; the school applies for you through the state scholarship system or the National Scholarship Portal.

name: PM YASASVI Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC, EBC and DNT Students
provider: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India
benefit: Pays compulsory course fees and a yearly allowance, from Class 11 up to PhD; amount depends on the course (verify on portal)
summary: For OBC, EBC and DNT students studying after Class 10 (Class 11-12, ITI, diploma, degree, PG) with family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh a year. In Tamil Nadu it reaches BC/MBC/DNC students through the state post-matric scholarship.
documents: Bonafide certificate from school or college
how_to_apply: Apply through your school or college after admission; in Tamil Nadu the college submits it on the state scholarship portal for you.

name: Central Sector Scheme of Scholarships for College and University Students
provider: Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, Government of India
benefit: Rs 12,000 per year for the first 3 years of a degree and Rs 20,000 per year for PG (and for the 4th/5th year of professional courses)
summary: For students who scored above the 80th percentile in their Class 12 board results and joined a regular (not correspondence) degree course, with family income up to Rs 4.5 lakh a year. The percentile cut-off is set by each board, so check your board's list.
documents: Bonafide certificate from school or college
how_to_apply: Register on the National Scholarship Portal in the same year you join college, and renew every year with your marks.
deadline_note: NSP usually opens between July and October

name: Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students
provider: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India
benefit: Full non-refundable course fees plus a yearly academic allowance of about Rs 2,500 to Rs 13,500 depending on the course (verify on portal)
summary: For SC students studying after Class 10 (Class 11 to PhD) with family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh a year. In Tamil Nadu it is given through the Adi Dravidar Welfare Department's scholarship, so you apply once.
documents: Bonafide certificate from school or college
how_to_apply: After you take admission, give your documents to your school or college scholarship office; they submit the application on the state portal.

name: Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Tribe Students
provider: Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India
benefit: Course fees plus a monthly maintenance allowance (about Rs 230 to Rs 1,200 depending on course and hostel; verify on portal)
summary: For ST students studying after Class 10 (Class 11 to PhD) with family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh a year.
documents: Bonafide certificate from school or college
how_to_apply: Apply on the National Scholarship Portal or your state portal after admission, and ask your college to verify it.

name: Pre-Matric Scholarship for SC and ST Students (Class 9-10)
provider: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment and Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India
benefit: SC: Rs 3,500 a year for day scholars and Rs 7,000 a year for hostel students; ST: about Rs 2,250 to Rs 5,250 a year (verify on portal)
summary: For SC and ST students in Class 9 and 10 whose family income is up to Rs 2.5 lakh a year.
documents: Bonafide certificate from school or college
how_to_apply: Your school applies for you; give your community and income certificates and bank details to the headmaster.

name: Pre-Matric Scholarship for Minorities (Class 9-10)
provider: Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India
benefit: Fee support plus a small monthly maintenance allowance (verify on portal)
summary: For Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain and Parsi students in Class 9 and 10 with at least 50% marks in the previous exam and family income up to Rs 1 lakh a year.
documents: Bonafide certificate from school or college
how_to_apply: Register on the National Scholarship Portal and apply; your school must verify the form.
deadline_note: NSP usually opens between July and October

name: Post-Matric Scholarship for Minorities
provider: Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India
benefit: Admission and tuition fees (up to about Rs 7,000-10,000 a year) plus a maintenance allowance of about Rs 230 to Rs 1,200 a month (verify on portal)
summary: For minority-community students from Class 11 to PhD with at least 50% marks in the previous exam and family income up to Rs 2 lakh a year. 30% of the awards are kept for girls.
documents: Bonafide certificate from school or college
how_to_apply: Register on the National Scholarship Portal and apply after admission; your institution verifies it online.
deadline_note: NSP usually opens between July and October

name: AICTE Pragati Scholarship for Girl Students
provider: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE)
benefit: Rs 50,000 per year for every year of the course
summary: For girls admitted to the first year of an AICTE-approved diploma or degree course (or second year through lateral entry), with family income up to Rs 8 lakh a year. Up to two girls per family.
documents: Bonafide certificate from school or college
how_to_apply: After joining a diploma or engineering college, apply on the National Scholarship Portal under AICTE Pragati.
deadline_note: NSP usually opens between July and October

name: AICTE Saksham Scholarship for Specially-Abled Students
provider: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE)
benefit: Rs 50,000 per year for every year of the course
summary: For students with 40% or more disability admitted to an AICTE-approved diploma or degree course, with family income up to Rs 8 lakh a year.
how_to_apply: After joining your diploma or degree course, apply on the National Scholarship Portal under AICTE Saksham.
deadline_note: NSP usually opens between July and October

name: AICTE Swanath Scholarship
provider: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE)
benefit: Rs 50,000 per year for every year of the course
summary: For orphans, students who lost a parent to COVID-19, and wards of armed forces or CAPF personnel martyred in action, studying an AICTE-approved diploma or degree course, with family income up to Rs 8 lakh a year.
documents: Death certificate of parent(s) or martyr certificate
how_to_apply: Apply on the National Scholarship Portal under AICTE Swanath after joining your course.
deadline_note: NSP usually opens between July and October

name: INSPIRE Scholarship for Higher Education (INSPIRE-SHE)
provider: Department of Science and Technology, Government of India
benefit: Rs 80,000 per year (Rs 60,000 scholarship + Rs 20,000 summer research project) for up to 5 years
summary: For students in the top 1% of their Class 12 board (or with a top JEE/NEET rank or a national science olympiad award) who study a B.Sc, BS or integrated M.Sc in basic and natural sciences. Age 17 to 22.
documents: Top 1% eligibility certificate from your board
Bonafide certificate from school or college
Endorsement form signed by college principal
how_to_apply: After joining a B.Sc/BS course, register on the INSPIRE website and upload your marks and the college endorsement form.

name: Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme for Wards of Ex-Servicemen and CAPF
provider: Kendriya Sainik Board (Ministry of Defence) / Ministry of Home Affairs
benefit: Rs 2,500 a month for boys and Rs 3,000 a month for girls
summary: For children and widows of ex-servicemen, ex-Coast Guard and CAPF/Assam Rifles personnel joining the first year of a professional course (engineering, medicine, BBA, BCA, B.Pharm and similar) with at least 60% in Class 12, diploma or graduation.
documents: Ex-servicemen / CAPF service certificate of parent
Bonafide certificate from school or college
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Kendriya Sainik Board website (ex-servicemen) or the National Scholarship Portal (CAPF) in your first year of the course.

name: Scholarships for Students with Disabilities (Pre-Matric and Post-Matric)
provider: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Government of India
benefit: Monthly allowance (about Rs 500 to Rs 1,600 depending on level) plus book and disability allowances; post-matric also covers fees (verify on portal)
summary: For students with 40% or more disability, from Class 9 to PG, with family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh a year.
documents: Bonafide certificate from school or college
how_to_apply: Register on the National Scholarship Portal, choose the disability scholarship for your class, and get it verified by your school or college.
deadline_note: NSP usually opens between July and October

name: Ishan Uday Special Scholarship for North Eastern Region
provider: University Grants Commission (UGC)
benefit: Rs 5,400 a month for general degree courses and Rs 7,800 a month for technical, medical and professional courses
summary: For students from the eight North Eastern states who passed Class 12 there and joined a regular degree course, with family income up to Rs 4.5 lakh a year.
documents: Bonafide certificate from school or college
how_to_apply: Apply on the National Scholarship Portal in your first year of college.
deadline_note: NSP usually opens between July and October

name: Pudhumai Penn (Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme)
provider: Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
benefit: Rs 1,000 a month until you finish your first degree, diploma or ITI course; given on top of other scholarships
summary: For girls who studied Class 6 to 12 in Tamil Nadu government schools (and, since December 2024, Tamil-medium government-aided schools) and join college, diploma, ITI or paramedical courses. No income limit.
how_to_apply: After joining college, ask your college's Pudhumai Penn nodal officer to register you on the portal; the money comes to your bank account every month.

name: Tamil Pudhalvan Scheme
provider: Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
benefit: Rs 1,000 a month until you finish your first degree, diploma or ITI course
summary: For boys who studied Class 6 to 12 in Tamil Nadu government schools (and Tamil-medium government-aided schools) and join a degree, diploma or ITI course. No income limit. Started in August 2024.
how_to_apply: After admission, your college registers you on the UMIS portal; the money is sent to your bank account every month.

name: Tamil Nadu Post-Matric Scholarship for BC, MBC and DNC Students
provider: Backward Classes, Most Backward Classes and Minorities Welfare Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
benefit: Tuition, special and exam fees paid for government and aided institutions, fixed fee amounts for self-financing colleges, plus a maintenance allowance (verify on portal)
summary: For BC, MBC and denotified community (DNC) students from Class 11 to PG in Tamil Nadu, with family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh a year. Some fee parts have no income limit for MBC and DNC students.
documents: Bonafide certificate from school or college
how_to_apply: Give your documents to your school or college scholarship section after admission; they apply for you on the state portal.

name: Tamil Nadu Post-Matric Scholarship for SC, ST and SC-Converted Christian Students
provider: Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
benefit: Full fees (tuition, special and exam fees) paid to the institution plus a maintenance allowance (verify on portal)
summary: For SC, ST and SC-converted-Christian students from Class 11 to PG in Tamil Nadu with family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh a year. This is how Tamil Nadu students get the central SC/ST post-matric scholarship.
documents: Bonafide certificate from school or college
how_to_apply: After admission, submit your documents to the college scholarship section; they apply on the state portal and the fee is paid directly.

name: Tamil Nadu First Graduate Tuition Fee Concession
provider: Higher Education Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
benefit: Full tuition fee waived for the whole course
summary: For students who are the first in their family to go to college and join a professional course (engineering, medicine, agriculture, veterinary, law and similar) through government single-window counselling. No income limit.
documents: Joint declaration by student and parent
how_to_apply: Get a first graduate certificate from the Tahsildar and upload it while applying for counselling (such as TNEA); the college then does not charge tuition fee.

name: HDFC Bank Parivartan's ECSS Programme
provider: HDFC Bank (CSR), run through Buddy4Study
benefit: Rs 15,000-18,000 for school, ITI and diploma students; Rs 30,000-50,000 for UG; Rs 35,000-75,000 for PG (verify on portal)
summary: Need-based scholarship for students from Class 1 to PG (including ITI and diploma) with at least 55% in the previous exam and family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh a year; students whose family faced a crisis in the last 3 years get priority.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Buddy4Study page for the programme; shortlisted students get a phone interview.

name: Reliance Foundation Undergraduate Scholarship
provider: Reliance Foundation
benefit: Up to Rs 2 lakh over the full degree, plus mentoring
summary: For first-year full-time undergraduate students in any stream with at least 60% in Class 12 and family income below Rs 15 lakh a year (income below Rs 2.5 lakh gets preference). Selection is through an online aptitude test.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Reliance Foundation Scholarships website in your first year of college and take the online aptitude test.

name: Tata Capital Pankh Scholarship Programme
provider: Tata Capital (CSR), run through Buddy4Study
benefit: Up to 80% of tuition fees, capped at about Rs 10,000-18,000 depending on the course (verify on portal)
summary: For Class 11-12, ITI, diploma and undergraduate students with at least 60% in the previous exam and family income up to Rs 2.5 lakh a year.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the Buddy4Study page for the Pankh programme; you need to apply again every year.
